newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says doctors recommend operation.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says doctors recommend operation.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, speaking slowly in a television interview, said Russian doctors had recommended that he have an operation on his heart.

"I want to have a society based on truth here, that means no longer hiding what we used to hide," he said in an interview shown on NTV commercial television. "I have undergone routine checks and during these checks they have found something wrong with my heart. Recomendations of doctors, our doctors, were for an operation or to work in a passive way."
Yeltsin, re-elected for a second four-year term in July, said he chose the operation because he could not agree to slow the pace of his work.
He said the operation was likely to take place in late September in an elite Moscow Cardiological centre, one of Russia's leading international medical centres.
"I do not want to go anywhere abroad," he said. "Our cardiological centre in Moscow is capable of performing such heart operations."

Yeltsin, who had two mild heart attacks last year, disappeared from the public eye in late June. His aides have said the 65-year-old Kremlin leader was overtired after a vigorous re-election campaign, but they denied he had any health problems.
